questions.stem: A 23-year-old man is brought to the clinic by his parents. For 9 months he has heard voices that comment on what he does. He believes his neighbors put cameras in his room. He speaks very little, shows almost no facial expression, and has stopped seeing friends and going to college. He does not use drugs, and a urine drug screen is negative. Thyroid tests, serum calcium and vitamin B12 are normal. Brain MRI shows no tumor or stroke. Which structural brain change is most consistently reported in groups of patients with this disorder?
choices: Atrophy of the heads of the caudate nuclei
Ovoid plaques in the periventricular white matter
Enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles
Hemorrhagic necrosis of the medial temporal lobes
questions.explanation: Hallucinations, a persecutory delusion and negative symptoms for more than 6 months point to **schizophrenia**. Its most consistent structural finding is **enlarged lateral and third ventricles**, with reduced cortical gray matter volume; these changes support the diagnosis but do not make it. **Caudate atrophy** also widens the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles, but it is typical of Huntington disease, which shows chorea and a family history. Periventricular plaques fit multiple sclerosis, mammillary body atrophy fits Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, and temporal necrosis fits HSV encephalitis.
questions.explanation_pt: Alucinações, um delírio persecutório e sintomas negativos por mais de 6 meses indicam **esquizofrenia**. O achado estrutural mais consistente é o **aumento dos ventrículos laterais e do terceiro ventrículo**, com redução do volume de substância cinzenta cortical; essas alterações apoiam o diagnóstico, mas não o confirmam. A **atrofia do caudado** também alarga os cornos frontais dos ventrículos laterais, mas é típica da doença de Huntington, que tem coreia e história familiar. Placas periventriculares sugerem esclerose múltipla, atrofia dos corpos mamilares sugere síndrome de Wernicke-Korsakoff e necrose temporal sugere encefalite herpética (HSV).

questions.stem: A 2-year-old girl is admitted for the fifth time in 6 months with fever and bacteremia. She has a long-term central venous catheter that was placed for IV antibiotics during an earlier admission. Her blood cultures have grown several different gut organisms, including Escherichia coli, Enterococcus faecalis and Klebsiella pneumoniae. The fevers start only during her mother's visits. During 3 weeks when a nurse stayed with the child all day, she had no fever. Her mother works as a medical assistant. The staff describe her as very caring, and she often asks for more tests. Work-up results: IgG, IgA and IgM are normal for age; absolute neutrophil count is 3,400/µL (normal); the dihydrorhodamine flow test is normal; HIV test is negative. Which diagnosis best describes the mother's behavior?
questions.explanation: Repeated infections with **different gut organisms** through a central line, a normal immune work-up, and fevers that occur only when the mother is present suggest that she **contaminates the catheter** on purpose. This is **factitious disorder imposed on another** (formerly *Munchausen syndrome by proxy*), a form of **child abuse**. The disorder is diagnosed in the person who produces the illness, so *factitious disorder imposed on self* does not fit the mother, who is not presenting herself as sick. Malingering needs an external gain such as money, and none is described.
questions.explanation_pt: Infecções repetidas por **diferentes bactérias intestinais** através de um cateter central, com investigação imunológica normal e febres que só ocorrem na presença da mãe, sugerem que ela **contamina o cateter** de propósito. Trata-se de **transtorno factício imposto a outro** (antiga *síndrome de Munchausen por procuração*), uma forma de **abuso infantil**. O diagnóstico é atribuído a quem produz a doença; por isso, *transtorno factício autoimposto* não se aplica à mãe, que não se apresenta como doente. A simulação exige um ganho externo, como dinheiro, e nenhum é descrito.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman comes to the clinic for abdominal pain, bloating and headaches that have bothered her for 2 years. She has made 14 emergency department visits in the past year. She spends several hours each day reading about her symptoms online and has stopped working because of them. An upper endoscopy and a colonoscopy last year were normal. Today her exam is normal. Laboratory results: hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, leukocytes 6,800/µL, C-reactive protein 2 mg/L (normal), TSH 1.8 µU/mL (normal), lipase normal, and celiac serology negative. She is not faking her symptoms and has no lawsuit or disability claim. Which approach is most appropriate?
choices: Order CT of the abdomen and pelvis to reassure her about serious disease
Refer her for a repeat colonoscopy with biopsies
Explain that her symptoms are not real and discharge her
Start a long-term opioid for her abdominal pain
Schedule regular brief visits with one primary care physician
questions.explanation: Real, distressing symptoms with **excessive time, worry and behavior** devoted to them, after a normal work-up, fit **somatic symptom disorder**. The best approach is **regular, scheduled visits with a single primary care physician**, who accepts that the symptoms are real and limits unnecessary tests; cognitive behavioral therapy can help. More imaging or a repeat colonoscopy is tempting for reassurance, but extra tests bring only short relief, add risk and reinforce the focus on disease. Telling her the symptoms are not real is wrong, because she is not producing them on purpose.
questions.explanation_pt: Sintomas reais e angustiantes, com **tempo, preocupação e comportamentos excessivos** dedicados a eles, após uma investigação normal, indicam **transtorno de sintomas somáticos**. A melhor conduta são **consultas regulares e agendadas com um único médico de atenção primária**, que reconhece que os sintomas são reais e limita exames desnecessários; a terapia cognitivo-comportamental pode ajudar. Mais exames de imagem ou uma nova colonoscopia são tentadores para tranquilizá-la, mas exames extras trazem alívio apenas passageiro, acrescentam riscos e reforçam o foco na doença. Dizer que os sintomas não são reais é errado, porque ela não os produz de propósito.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man has had a psychiatric illness for 3 years. In that time he has had two manic episodes, with little sleep, rapid speech and reckless spending, and one major depressive episode. Together these mood episodes have been present for most of the 3 years. During them, he also heard voices and believed he was being followed. For the past 5 weeks his mood has been normal: he sleeps well, his energy is normal and he enjoys his hobbies. However, he still hears voices that insult him and still believes the police are following him. He does not use drugs, and medical tests are normal. Which diagnosis is most likely?
choices: Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features
Major depressive disorder with psychotic features
questions.explanation: Psychosis that continues for **at least 2 weeks with a normal mood**, together with major mood episodes that fill **most of the illness**, is **schizoaffective disorder** (bipolar type here). Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features is the most tempting choice, but in that disorder psychosis appears **only during** mood episodes. Schizophrenia is less likely because his mood episodes are present for most of the total illness, not just a small part of it.
questions.explanation_pt: Psicose que persiste por **pelo menos 2 semanas com humor normal**, junto com episódios depressivos maiores ou maníacos presentes na **maior parte da doença**, é **transtorno esquizoafetivo** (aqui do tipo bipolar). O transtorno bipolar tipo I com sintomas psicóticos é a opção mais tentadora, mas nele a psicose aparece **apenas durante** os episódios de humor. A esquizofrenia é menos provável porque os episódios de humor ocupam a maior parte da doença, e não apenas uma pequena parte dela.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old engineer comes to the clinic because his wife insists. She says he makes detailed lists and rules for every household task and becomes angry when she loads the dishwasher "the wrong way." At work he often misses deadlines because he rewrites his reports until they are perfect, and he will not let colleagues help because they "will not do it right." He rarely takes a day off. He says his standards are correct and that others should simply be more careful. He has no intrusive thoughts, and he does not perform rituals to relieve anxiety. These traits have been present since early adulthood. Which diagnosis is most likely?
questions.explanation: A lifelong pattern of **perfectionism**, rigid rules, devotion to work and refusal to delegate, which the patient sees as **correct** (*ego-syntonic*), is **obsessive-compulsive personality disorder** (cluster C). Obsessive-compulsive disorder is the tempting choice, but it involves unwanted **obsessions** and **compulsions** that the patient sees as excessive and distressing (*ego-dystonic*), and he has neither. Narcissistic patients need admiration and lack empathy; their main goal is not order and control.
questions.explanation_pt: Um padrão duradouro de **perfeccionismo**, regras rígidas, dedicação excessiva ao trabalho e recusa em delegar, que o paciente considera **correto** (*egossintônico*), é **transtorno da personalidade obsessivo-compulsiva** (grupo C). O transtorno obsessivo-compulsivo é a opção tentadora, mas envolve **obsessões** e **compulsões** indesejadas, que o paciente reconhece como excessivas e angustiantes (*egodistônico*), e ele não tem nenhuma delas. Pacientes narcisistas precisam de admiração e não têm empatia; seu objetivo principal não é a ordem e o controle.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman learns that her divorce is final. When a friend asks how she feels, she says, "I'm fine, I don't want to talk about it." That same weekend she spends most of her savings at a casino, drives home far above the speed limit and has unprotected sex with two men she has just met. She has never had a manic episode, and she slept normally all weekend. Later she says she does not know why she did these things. Which defense mechanism best explains her behavior?
questions.explanation: **Acting out** is an immature defense in which a person expresses an unbearable feeling through **impulsive actions** instead of noticing or talking about it. Here the pain of the divorce is turned into gambling, reckless driving and risky sex. **Displacement** is tempting, but it redirects a feeling toward a **safer target** (for example, yelling at a coworker instead of the ex-husband), and there is no such target here. Her "I'm fine" is only an avoidance of talking; **denial** would mean refusing to accept the reality of the divorce or its pain, and her extreme behavior shows that the pain is being expressed in action.
questions.explanation_pt: **Atuação** (*acting out*) é um mecanismo de defesa imaturo em que a pessoa expressa um sentimento insuportável por meio de **ações impulsivas**, em vez de percebê-lo ou falar sobre ele. Aqui, a dor do divórcio se transforma em jogos de azar, direção imprudente e sexo de risco. O **deslocamento** é tentador, mas redireciona um sentimento para um **alvo mais seguro** (por exemplo, gritar com um colega em vez de com o ex-marido), e não há esse alvo aqui. O "estou bem" é apenas uma forma de evitar o assunto; a **negação** significaria recusar-se a aceitar a realidade do divórcio ou da dor, e o comportamento extremo mostra que a dor está sendo expressa em ações.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman comes to the clinic because of strange episodes over the past 8 months. Several times a week, she feels as if she is watching herself from outside her body, like a character in a film. Her hands do not feel like her own, and the world looks flat and unreal. She says, "I know it is only a feeling, but it scares me that I might be going crazy." The episodes do not come with a racing heart, chest pain or fear of dying. She does not use drugs, and a urine drug screen is negative. She can recall all events of her life. Neurologic exam and EEG are normal. Which diagnosis is most likely?
questions.explanation: Recurrent feelings of being **detached from one's own body** (depersonalization) and of the world being **unreal** (derealization), with **intact reality testing** (she knows it is only a feeling), point to **depersonalization/derealization disorder**. Panic attacks can also cause depersonalization, but here the episodes occur without palpitations, chest pain or fear of dying. In schizophrenia, reality testing is lost, and she has no delusions or hallucinations. She has no memory gaps or separate identities, so dissociative amnesia and dissociative identity disorder do not fit.
questions.explanation_pt: Sensações recorrentes de estar **separada do próprio corpo** (despersonalização) e de que o mundo é **irreal** (desrealização), com **teste de realidade preservado** (ela sabe que é apenas uma sensação), indicam **transtorno de despersonalização/desrealização**. Ataques de pânico também podem causar despersonalização, mas aqui os episódios ocorrem sem palpitações, dor torácica ou medo de morrer. Na esquizofrenia, o teste de realidade está perdido, e ela não tem delírios nem alucinações. Ela não tem lacunas de memória nem identidades distintas, então amnésia dissociativa e transtorno dissociativo de identidade não se aplicam.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man is evaluated in prison. He has been arrested many times for fighting, car theft and fraud. He has used several false names to get loans that he never repaid. He calmly describes beating a man in a robbery and says, "He should have handed over his wallet faster." He shows no guilt. He has never had a manic episode or psychotic symptoms. To diagnose his most likely personality disorder, his records must show evidence of which condition before age 15?
questions.explanation: A pervasive pattern of crime, lying, aggression and **lack of remorse** in an adult points to **antisocial personality disorder** (cluster B). The diagnosis requires age **18 or older** and evidence of **conduct disorder before age 15**: aggression to people or animals, destruction of property, theft or serious rule-breaking. Oppositional defiant disorder is the tempting choice, but defiance toward authority without violating the basic rights of others is not enough. ADHD is common in these patients, but it is not a required criterion.
questions.explanation_pt: Um padrão persistente de crimes, mentiras, agressividade e **ausência de remorso** em um adulto indica **transtorno da personalidade antissocial** (grupo B). O diagnóstico exige idade de **18 anos ou mais** e evidência de **transtorno de conduta antes dos 15 anos**: agressão a pessoas ou animais, destruição de propriedade, furto ou violação grave de regras. O transtorno de oposição desafiante é a opção tentadora, mas desafiar a autoridade sem violar os direitos básicos dos outros não basta. O TDAH é comum nesses pacientes, mas não é um critério obrigatório.
